summary: CLI iterations reach main’s repetition control; CSR setup closes the terminal offset at n=floor(dim²/sparsity). The `spmvGpu` dispatcher selects subgroup widths 1/2/4/8/16/32 by average row length, or the 256-thread long-row kernel at average>=512. Short-row launches use ceil(dim/(128/width)) blocks, covering each row exactly once; each width kernel traverses its entire CSR interval in width strides, reduces and writes the row. Long rows launch one block for every row; its threads process the full CSR interval in blockDim strides and reduce/store. A synchronized warmup is outside timing. The timed graph captures min(iterations,128) calls when batch>1; compiled main launches graph batches while subtracting 128 (or the actual batch) until below the bound, then loops through the exact remaining direct calls. Start/end events and completion sync bracket those calls. Compiled `spmvGpu` dispatch and all width/long-row launch paths were followed through actual cudaLaunchKernel helpers. All seven native sm86 kernels were checked through arithmetic backedges, reductions/stores and exits. No omission identified.
